failures.criterion: 2 Closed pull requests, with the spec's shared rule that no run posts skipped results at a head another run tests: closing cancels the pull request's waiting runs, and a reopen must still get its own full run
failures.evidence: A closed run GitHub creates after a quick reopen cancels the reopened pull request's runs. On #2375: `gh pr close 2375` (closed 06:54:46Z), `gh pr reopen 2375` (reopened 06:54:48Z). The reopened Legion Envoy and Contracts run 40463925526 was created 06:54:50Z; the Envoy closed run 40463967410 was created only at 06:55:14Z, entered envoy-and-contracts-2375 and cancelled 40463925526 at 06:55:15Z (annotation on job 122054715920: 'Canceling since a higher priority waiting request for envoy-and-contracts-2375 exists'). The open pull request's head cbf6e85b then shows changes/envoy-go and every Envoy job skipped (check runs 122054846993, 122054847519) and no Envoy run. Before this change a reopen always ran in full, because a close started no run. The same order for Tests (tests-closed.yaml's cancel-tests created after the reopened Tests run) would cancel the reopened lint/typecheck/test [INFERENCE: same group mechanism, not observed in this run; in all three cycles cancel-tests was created first]; that fails closed but blocks the merge until a push. Two cycles 5-8 s apart kept the right order. The PR body residual and the tests-closed.yaml comment ('On a reopen ... That is harmless') cover only the other order. No red test is committed: the defect is GitHub's run-creation order racing a reopen, which no suite in the repository can reproduce, and a test that reads the workflow text is a source-text test; the run ids above pin it. Fix shapes for the architect: (a) accept and document the race as a residual (PR body, tests-closed.yaml comment, docs); (b) replace the closed-event concurrency cancels with one closed-event job that cancels this pull request's pull_request runs created before github.event.pull_request.closed_at (race-free, needs actions: write and one runner job per close).
